record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:33a805f7.help: Contact interface ID. This must be a unique number.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:862cf498.help: Interface descriptor. It is suggested that unique descriptions be used.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:ced317ff.help:
Segment set ID, node set ID, part set ID, part ID, shell element set ID,or branch ID for specifying the SURFA side of the contact interface (see Setting the Contact Interface). See *SET_SEGMENT, *SET_NODE_OPTION, *PART, *SET_PART or *SET_SHELL_OPTION. For ERODING_SINGLE_SURFACE and ERODING_SURFACE_TO_SURFACE contact types, use either a part ID or a part set ID. For ERODING_NODES_TO_SURFACE contact, use a node set that includes all nodes that may be exposed to contact as element erosion occurs. 
EQ.0: Includes all parts in the case of single surface contact types

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:8862ee7f.help:
Segment set ID, part set ID, part ID, shell element set ID, or branch ID for the SURFB side of the contact (see Setting the Contact Interface).
EQ.0: SURFB side is not applicable for single surface contact types.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:8d697c51.help:
The ID type of SURFA:
EQ.0: segment set ID for surface to surface contact,
EQ.1: shell element set ID for surface to surface contact,
EQ.2: part set ID,
EQ.3: part ID,
EQ.4: node set ID for node to surface contact,
EQ.5: include all (SURFA field is ignored),
EQ.6: part set ID for exempted parts. All non-exempted parts are included in the contact.
EQ.7: Branch ID; see *SET_PART_TREE

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:6d17855b.help:
ID type of SURFB:
EQ.0: segment set ID,
EQ.1: shell element set ID,
EQ.2: part set ID,
EQ.3: part ID,
EQ.5:Include all ( SURFB Field is ignored).
EQ.6: Part set ID for exempted parts.  All non-exempted parts are included in the contact.
EQ.7: Branch ID; see *SET_PART_TREE

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:46d0b83b.help: Include in the contact definition only those SURFA nodes/segments within box SABOXID (corresponding to BOXID in *DEFINE_BOX), or if SABOXID is negative, only those SURFA nodes/segments within contact volume |SABOXID | (corresponding to CVID in *DEFINE_CONTACT_VOLUME). SABOXID can be used only if SURFATYP is set to 2, 3, 5, or 6, meaning, SURFA is a part ID or part set ID. SABOXID is not available for ERODING contact types

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:9c764857.help: Include in the contact definition only those SURFB segments within box SBBOXID (corresponding to BOXID in *DEFINE_BOX), or if SBBOXID is negative, only those SURFB segments within contact volume |SBBOXID | (corresponding to CVID in *DEFINE_CONTACT_VOLUME). SBBOXID can be used only if SURFBTYP is set to 2, 3, 5,or 6, meaning, SURFB is a part ID or part set ID.  SBBOXID is not available for ERODING contact types.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:52941ba7.help:
Include the SURFA side in the *DATABASE_NCFORC and the *DATABASE_BINARY_INTFOR interface force files, and optionally in the dynain file for wear:
EQ.0: Do not include.
EQ.1: SURFA side forces included.
EQ.2: Same as 1 but also allows SURFA nodes to be written as *INITIAL_CONTACT_WEAR to dynain; see NCYC on *INTERFACE_SPRINGBACK_LSDYNA.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:0ce0ad1c.help:
Include the SURFB side in the *DATABASE_NCFORC and the *DATABASE_BINARY_INTFOR interface force files, and optionally in the dynain file for wear:
EQ.0: Do not include.
EQ.1: SURFB side forces included.
EQ.2: Same as 1, but also allows SURFB nodes to be written as *INITIAL_CONTACT_WEAR to dynain; see NCYC on *INTERFACE_SPRINGBACK_LSDYNA.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:9afaf689.help:
Static coefficient of friction. If FS is > 0 and not equal to 2. The frictional coefficient is assumed to be dependent on the relative velocity Vrel of the surfaces in contact according to the equation in the manual.
The three other possibilities are:
EQ.2: For a subset of SURFACE_TO_SURFACE type contacts (see Remark 1 below), FD is a table ID (see *DEFINE_TABLE). That table specifies two or more values of contact pressure, with each pressure value in the table corresponding to a curve of friction coefficient as a function of relative velocity. Thus, the friction coefficient becomes a function of pressure and relative velocity. See Figure 0-2.
EQ.-2: If only one friction table is defined using *DEFINE_FRICTION, it will be used, and there is no need to specify parameter FD. If more than one friction table is defined, the friction table ID is defined by FD below.
EQ.-1: If the frictional coefficients defined in the *PART section are to be used, set FS to -1.0.
WARNING: The FS = -1.0 and F = -2.0 options apply only to contact types:
SINGLE_SURFACE
AIRBAG_SINGLE_SURFACE
AUTOMATIC_GENERAL
AUTOMATIC_SINGLE_SURFACE
AUTOMATIC_SINGLE_SURFACE_MORTAR
AUTOMATIC_NODES_TO_SURFACE
AUTOMATIC_SURFACE_TO_SURFACE
AUTOMATIC_SURFACE_TO_SURFACE_MORTAR
AUTOMATIC_ONE_WAY_SURFACE_TO_SURFACE
ERODING_SINGLE_SURFACE

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:a3eb5bac.help:
Dynamic coefficient of friction. If FS > 0 and not equal to 2, the frictional coefficient is assumed to be dependent on the relative velocity Vrel of the surfaces in contact according to the equation in the manual.
Otherwise:
FS.EQ.-2: Friction table ID if more than one friction table is defined
FS.EQ.2: Table ID for a table that specifies two or more values of contact pressure, with each pressure value in the table corresponding to a curve of friction coefficient as a function of relative velocity.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:8ae49c2f.help: Exponential decay coefficient. The frictional coefficient is assumed to depend on the relative velocity v-rel of the surfaces in contact. (default=0.0).

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:ab867539.help: Coefficient for viscous friction. This is necessary to limit the friction force to a maximum.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:a955772f.help: Viscous damping coefficient in percent of critical. To avoid undesirable oscillation in contact, e.g., for sheet forming simulation, a contact damping perpendicular to the contacting surfaces is applied.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:77a7ec1a.help: Small penetration in the contact search option.  If the tracked node penetrates more than the segment thickness times the factor XPENE (see *CONTROL_CONTACT), the penetration is ignored, and the tracked node is set free.  The thickness is taken as the shell thickness if the segment belongs to a shell element or it is taken as 1/20 of its shortest diagonal if the segment belongs to a solid element.  This option applies to the surface-to-surface contact algorithms.  See Table 0-17 for contact types and more details.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:0310444a.help: Birth time (contact surface becomes active at this time):LT.0: Birth time is set to | "BT" | .When negative, birth time is followed during the dynamic relaxation phase of the calculation.After the completion of dynamic relaxation, contact is activated regardless of the value of BT.EQ.0: Birth time is inactive, meaning contact is always activeGT.0: If DT = -9999, BT is interpreted as the curve or table ID defining multiple pairs of birth - time / death - time; see Remark 2 below.Otherwise, if "DT" > 0, birth time applies both duringand after dynamic relaxation.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:cb71f5ce.help: Death time (contact surface is deactivated at this time):LT.0: If DT = -9999, BT is interpreted as the curve or table ID defining multiple pairs of birth - time / death - time.Otherwise, negative DT indicates that contact is inactive during dynamic relaxation.After dynamic relaxation the birth and death times are followed and set to | "BT" | and | "DT" | , respectively.EQ.0: DT defaults to 10e20.GT.0: DT sets the time at which the contact is deactivated.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:719f5903.help:
Scale factor on default SURFA penalty stiffness when SOFT = 0 or SOFT = 2; see also *CONTROL_CONTACT.For MORTAR frictional contact this is the stiffness scale factor for the entire contact, and SFSB does not apply.
LT.0: -SFSA gives the load curve ID for contact pressure as a function of penetration depth. This is supported for Mortar contact only.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:c6761484.help: Scale factor on default SURFB penalty stiffness when SOFT = 0 or SOFT = 2; see also *CONTROL_CONTACT.For MORTAR tied contact, this is an additional stiffness scale factor, resulting in a total stiffness scale of SFSA*SFSB.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:d5979756.help: Optional thickness for SURFA surface (overrides true thickness). This option applies only to contact with shell elements. SAST has no bearing on the actual thickness of the elements; it only affects the location of the contact surface. For the *CONTACT_TIED_.. options, SAST and SBST below can be defined as negative values, which will cause the determination of whether or not a node is tied to depend only on the separation distance relative to the absolute value of these thicknesses. More information is given under General Remarks on *CONTACT following Optional Card C.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:ab229ff0.help: Optional thickness for SURFB surface (overrides true thickness). This option applies only to contact with shell elements. True thickness is the element thickness of the shell elements. For the TIED options see SAST above.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:882c2bfb.help: Scale factor applied to the contact thickness of the SURFA surface.  This option applies to contact with shell and beam elements.  SFSAT has no bearing on the actual thickness of the elements; it only affects the location of the contact surface.  SFSAT is ignored if SAST is nonzero except in the case of MORTAR contact (see Remark 14 in the General Remarks: *Contact section).

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:b5a89ce2.help: Scale factor applied to the contact thickness of the SURFB surface.  This option applies only to contact with shell elements.  SFSBT has no bearing on the actual thickness of the elements; it only affects the location of the contact surface. SFSBT is ignored if SBST is nonzero except in the case of MORTAR contact (see Remark 14 in the General Remarks: *Contact section).

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:aa831cf8.help: Coulomb friction scale factor (default=1.0).The Coulomb friction value is scaled as _sc=FSF_c; see Mandatory Card 2.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:d1ef2bcd.help: Viscous friction scale factor (default=1.0).If this factor is defined, the limiting force becomes: F_lim =VSFVCA_cont ; see Mandatory Card 2.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:f494b45c.help:
Static coefficient of friction in the local n orthotropic direction for the
SURFA (SA) or SURFB (SB) surface. The frictional coefficient is assumed
to be dependent on the relative velocity of the surfaces in contact, 
where the direction and surface are left off for clarity

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:96e7382c.help: Dynamic coefficient of friction in the local n orthotropic direction

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:2e8cd485.help: Exponential decay coefficient for the local n direction

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:ee1fc84f.help: Coefficient for viscous friction in the local n direction. See the description for VC for mandatory Card 2 above

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:fb23da0f.help:
The table ID of a two dimensional table, see *DEFINE_TABLE or
*DEFINE_TABLE_2D, giving the friction coefficient in the local n
direction as a function of the relative velocity and interface pressure.
In this case, each curve in the table definition defines the coefficient
of friction versus the interface pressure corresponding to a particular value of the relative velocity

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:e0a5a47f.help:
If the default value, 0, is active, the frictional forces acting on a node
sliding on a segment are based on the local directions of the segment.
If OACS is set to unity, 1, the frictional forces acting on a
node sliding on a segment are based on the local directions of the
sliding node. No matter what the setting for OACS, the _SA coefficients
are always used for SURFA nodes and the _SB coefficients for SURFB nodes.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:e550e8d7.help:
Model for shear response. See the equations in the Remarks for details.
EQ.1: limiting shear stress depends on CIDMU in both tension and compression. See remark 3.
EQ.2: limiting shear stress depends on CIDETA in tension and CIDMU in compression. See remark 4.
EQ.3: limiting shear stress depends on CIDETA in both tension and compression. See remark 5..

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:c0ae6628.help: Curve ID for the coefficient of friction ()  as a function of the Hershey number H.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:60e67209.help: Curve ID for the viscosity (T) as a function of temperature T.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:f1b50901.help: Maximum strain the blank will experience when it passes the bead

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:041542b1.help: Scale factor to weaken the stress-strain curve

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:2301d813.help: Parameter to define the length of the bead ends during which the weakening effect will phase out

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:2f90e8ec.help: Load curve ID defining the plastic strain versus the parametric coordinate through the shell thickness. The parametric coordinate should be defined in the interval between -1 and 1 inclusive.  The value of plastic strain at the integration point is interpolated from this load curve. If the plastic strain at an integration point exceeds the value of the load curve at the time initialization occurs, the plastic strain at the point will remain unchanged.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:56785685.help: Scale factor that multiplies the shell thickness as the shell element moves under the draw bead.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:98be79de.help: Optional load curve ID defining the plastic strain versus the parametric coordinate through the shell thickness, which is used after an element has traveled a distance equal to OFFSET. The parametric coordinate should be defined in the interval between -1 and 1 inclusive. The value of plastic strain at the integration point is interpolated from this load curve. If the plastic strain at an integration point exceeds the value of the load curve at the time initialization occurs, the plastic strain at the point will remain unchanged. Input parameters LCEPS2 and OFFSET provide a way to model the case where a material moves under two draw beads. In this latter case the curve would be the sum of the plastic strains generated by moving under two consecutive beads.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:49f336df.help: If the center of an element has moved a distance equal to OFFSET, the load curve ID, LCEPS2 is used to reinitiialize the plastic strain. The TSCALE scale factor is also applied.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:e77b848e.help:
Symmetry plane option:
EQ.0: off (default),
EQ.1: Do not include faces with normal boundary constraints (such as segments of brick elements on a symmetry plane).
This option is important to retain the correct boundary conditions in the model with symmetry.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:e3039be8.help:
Erosion/Interior node option:
EQ.0: only exterior boundary information is saved,
EQ.1: storage is allocated so that eroding contact can occur. Otherwise, no contact is assumed after erosion of the corresponding element.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:eea09090.help:
Adjacent material treatment for solid elements:
EQ.0: solid element faces are included only for free boundaries,
EQ.1: solid element faces are included if they are on the boundary of the material subset. This option also allows the erosion within a body and the subsequent treatment of contact.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:a452cbfd.help: The method option for the gap function

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:27e47110.help: x component of the free sliding direction Tslide.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:ce6c3149.help: y component of the free sliding direction Tslide

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:8bbd83eb.help: z component of the free sliding direction Tslide.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:1c7e7379.help: Shear stress at failure. See FS

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:a417a1f1.help: Exponential decay coefficient. The frictional coefficient is assumed to be dependent on the relative velocity v-rel of the surfaces in contact. (default=0.0).

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:6d38f2f2.help: Coefficient for viscous friction. This is necessary to limit the friction force to a maximum.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:a2cee2c3.help: Viscous damping coefficient in percent of critical. In order to avoid undesirable oscillation in contact, e.g., for sheet forming simulation, a contact damping perpendicular to the contacting surfaces is applied.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:eadfa75e.help: Small penetration in contact search option.  If the slave node penetrates more than the segment thickness times the factor XPENE (see *CONTROL_CONTACT), the penetration is ignored, and the slave node is set free.  The thickness is taken as the shell thickness if the segment belongs to a shell element or it is taken as 1/20 of its shortest diagonal if the segment belongs to a solid element.  This option applies to the surface-to-surface contact algorithms.  See Table 0-17 for contact types and more details.

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:b26f2246.help: Birth time when contact surface becomes active. (default=0.0).

record:3c11134d2da44eeb1b070a21:6bf87d98.help: Death time when contact surface is deactivated (default=1.0E+20).
